    – Under the Dodd-Frank Act, the Financial Stability Oversight Council (FSOC) recommends and the Federal Reserve imposes enhanced prudential standards on systemically important bank holding companies (GSIBs).     – Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1), Tier 1 and Total capital ratios, each against risk-weighted assets, with three add-ons:  
      • A GSIB surcharge (4.5% under Method 2 for JPMorgan Chase & Co.)  
      • A capital conservation buffer (2.5% for Advanced approaches; standardized firms face a 2.5% “SCB”)  
      • A countercyclical capital buffer (currently set to 0%).  
    – These requirements apply both at the holding-company level (per Federal Reserve rules) and to JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. (per FDIC Improvement Act rules, though the bank itself is not subject to the GSIB surcharge).

 •  Manufacturing capabilities  
 •  Processor pricing and total system costs  

NVIDIA notes that its ability to “anticipate the features and functions that customers and partners will demand” and then deliver “consistent volumes … at acceptable levels of quality and at competitive prices” will determine its success.
